newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: First Mozambican cases of river blindness detected.
newsitem.headline: First Mozambican cases of river blindness detected.

text.p: River blindness has been detected in Mozambique for the first time, the national board of health said on Tuesday.
A research team found cases of the disease, which is caused by a parasitic worm, in Milange district of central Mozambique, on the border with southeastern Malawi, the board said in a statement.
River blindness was well-documented in Malawi but had not been recorded before in Mozambique.
Hundreds of thousands of people fled Mozambique's 16-year civil war for Malawi and returned after a peace deal in in 1992.
The research team at the medical faculty of Eduardo Mondlane University in Maputo said it was possible they had brought the disease with them, but it did not say how many cases had been found.
Over 90 percent of the world's cases of river blindness are recorded in tropical Africa.
